svg.text: Folded at 15 minutes, the noise averages out and a sawtooth is left: the frequency climbs through each quarter-hour and drops right after it turns, most at the full hour (red).
Power is traded in blocks (since October 2025 the day-ahead market clears quarter-hours), so power plants ramp their schedules in steps at the boundaries while demand
changes smoothly: the mismatch shows up as frequency, and primary control has to catch it. These are the 'deterministic frequency deviations' grid operators know well. Caveat:
one day; the sign and size change with the season and the hour of day.
